title: Table Styles Showcase
author: SnapLogic

sections.title: Simple Style (Default)
sections.content:
The **simple** style features a navy header with white text and alternating row colors (white/light gray). This is the default style, suitable for most general-purpose tables.

[TABLE:simple:Platform Tier Feature Comparison]
| Feature | Basic | Professional | Enterprise |
|---------|-------|--------------|------------|
| API Calls/Month | 10K | 100K | Unlimited |
| Data Processing | 1GB | 100GB | Unlimited |
| Support | Email | Email + Chat | 24/7 Phone |
| SLA | 99% | 99.5% | 99.9% |
| Custom Connectors | No | 5 | Unlimited |
[/TABLE]

As shown in Table 1, the simple style provides clear visual hierarchy with minimal distraction.

sections.title: Minimal Style
sections.content:
The **minimal** style uses horizontal rules only (booktabs style) with no colored backgrounds. Ideal for technical specifications and academic-style documents where color would be distracting.

[TABLE:minimal:System Requirements Specification]
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Maximum |
|-----------|---------|-------------|----------|
| CPU | 2 cores | 4 cores | 16 cores |
| RAM | 4GB | 16GB | 128GB |
| Storage | 50GB SSD | 250GB SSD | 2TB NVMe |
| Network | 100Mbps | 1Gbps | 10Gbps |
[/TABLE]

Table 2 demonstrates the clean, professional appearance of the minimal style.

sections.title: Accent Styles
sections.content:
**Accent styles** use colored headers (blue, jade, or orange) with white backgrounds. Perfect for feature highlights, pricing tiers, and callout tables.

**Blue Accent (Information):**

[TABLE:accent-blue:API Endpoints Overview]
| Endpoint | Method | Rate Limit | Auth Required |
|----------|--------|------------|---------------|
| /users | GET | 1000/hour | Yes |
| /data | POST | 500/hour | Yes |
| /status | GET | Unlimited | No |
[/TABLE]

**Jade Accent (Success/Recommended):**

[TABLE:accent-jade:Recommended Configuration]
| Setting | Value | Impact | Priority |
|---------|-------|--------|----------|
| Cache Size | 2GB | High | Critical |
| Timeout | 30s | Medium | High |
| Retries | 3 | Low | Medium |
[/TABLE]

**Orange Accent (Warning/Attention):**

[TABLE:accent-orange:Critical Maintenance Windows]
| Date | System | Duration | Impact |
|------|--------|----------|--------|
| May 1 | Database | 4 hours | High |
| May 15 | API Gateway | 2 hours | Medium |
[/TABLE]

Tables 3-5 show how accent colors convey semantic meaning.

sections.title: Bordered Style
sections.content:
The **bordered** style adds cell borders throughout, with a light gray header. Useful for reference tables, error code lookups, and complex multi-column data where clear cell boundaries aid scanning.

[TABLE:bordered:HTTP Status Code Reference]
| Code | Category | Meaning | Common Use |
|------|----------|---------|------------|
| 200 | Success | OK | Successful request |
| 201 | Success | Created | Resource created |
| 400 | Client Error | Bad Request | Invalid syntax |
| 401 | Client Error | Unauthorized | Auth required |
| 404 | Client Error | Not Found | Resource missing |
| 500 | Server Error | Internal Error | Server failure |
[/TABLE]

Table 6 illustrates how borders help with dense reference data.

sections.title: Status Style
sections.content:
The **status** style uses row colors to indicate semantic states, with the first column bolded for row labels. Perfect for project status, timeline tables, and requirement tracking.

[TABLE:status-jade,jade,orange,blue]
| Task | Owner | Due Date | Status |
|------|-------|----------|--------|
| API Migration | DevOps | 2026-05-15 | Complete |
| Security Audit | InfoSec | 2026-05-01 | Complete |
| Documentation | Tech Writers | 2026-04-30 | In Progress |
| Performance Test | QA Team | 2026-05-10 | Not Started |
[/TABLE]

Table 7 uses color-coded rows: jade (complete), orange (in progress), blue (not started).

sections.title: Financial Data Example
sections.content:
Tables work well with financial data. The simple style provides a clean presentation:

[TABLE:simple:Quarterly Financial Performance 2026]
| Quarter | Revenue | Expenses | Profit | Growth |
|---------|---------|----------|--------|--------|
| Q1 2026 | $1.2M | $800K | $400K | 15% |
| Q2 2026 | $1.5M | $900K | $600K | 25% |
| Q3 2026 | $1.8M | $950K | $850K | 20% |
| Q4 2026 | $2.1M | $1.1M | $1.0M | 17% |
| **Total** | **$6.6M** | **$3.75M** | **$2.85M** | **19%** |
[/TABLE]

Table 8 shows financial data with totals row in bold.

sections.title: Style Selection Guide
sections.content:
**When to use each style:**

[TABLE:minimal:Table Style Decision Matrix]
| Style | Best For | Visual Weight | Use Case |
|-------|----------|---------------|----------|
| simple | General data | Medium | Default choice |
| minimal | Technical specs | Low | Dense numeric data |
| accent-blue | Information | Medium-High | Feature highlights |
| accent-jade | Success/Recommended | Medium-High | Pricing tiers |
| accent-orange | Warnings | Medium-High | Attention needed |
| bordered | Reference data | High | Lookup tables |
| status | Project tracking | Variable | Status dashboards |
[/TABLE]

Table 9 helps choose the appropriate style for your content.
